paras: The Regulator attack on Black ore-diggers at Hunnewell Furnace was a night clash on March 20, 1881, at Browntown, Greenup County, Kentucky, between about twelve or fifteen Regulators and a party of Black workers hired by the furnace. One Black man was wounded in the face and one Regulator was shot, and eight of the band were later reported jailed at Catlettsburg. A Grayson dispatch presented the clash as part of a Regulator "reign of terror" around Grayson and in adjoining Greenup County.

According to the dispatch, a party of men had tried to "control the business action" of the furnace company, four miles below Grayson on the Eastern Kentucky Railroad. Early in March, Superintendent Sebastian Gifort sent his son Joseph to Virginia, and the son returned with about forty Black men to dig ore. The hiring "incensed the so-called Regulators," who sent the Giforts anonymous notices to leave the country or face death.

On the night of the 20th, about twelve or fifteen Regulators met a party of the Black ore-diggers in Browntown, near the furnace, and "a brisk fight ensued" with several shots fired. One Black man received a face wound and a Regulator named Jones was shot through the groin; the dispatch does not say who fired first. The workers fell back to the furnace, and Gifort armed about two hundred employees.

Armed men then guarded the property day and night against threats of death and fire. Eight of the band were reported jailed at Catlettsburg; no report of a trial or of the wounded worker's name was found.

The coverage found is one Grayson dispatch, printed by the Wheeling Register on March 31 as "KENTUCKY REGULATORS" and by the Lexington Kentucky Gazette on April 2. The Gazette headlined it "ROUGH RIDERS. BAD WORK OF KENTUCKY REGULATORS" with the deck "Furnace in a State of Siege—Fight With Black Ore-Diggers." Told from the company's side, the story called the band "irresponsible ruffians" and the workers "negroes" and "blacks," naming none of them.
Both papers paired the clash with a separate Regulator whipping of a man named Bellamy and his family for "alleged immorality," framing it as rural vigilantism.

reader.title: Regulator attack on Black ore-diggers at Hunnewell Furnace
bases: A band styling itself 'Regulators' sent anonymous notices threatening death to the furnace managers for employing about forty Black ore-diggers and then fought a party of those workers at night (A1, A2).
Both printings carry the same Grayson, Ky., dispatch nearly word for word (A1, A2); no independent account, local report or follow-up was found.

accounts.label: Grayson, Ky., wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Regulators angered by the hiring of Black ore-diggers threatened the managers, met a party of the workers at Browntown on the night of the 20th, and in the fight that followed one Black man and one Regulator were wounded; the furnace armed its men and eight Regulators were jailed.

framing.detail: The Kentucky Gazette headlined 'ROUGH RIDERS. BAD WORK OF KENTUCKY REGULATORS' and 'Furnace in a State of Siege'; the dispatch called the band 'irresponsible ruffians' and took the company's side.
The Wheeling Register ran the dispatch under 'KENTUCKY REGULATORS / Inaugurate a Reign of Terror in Certain Localities', without the paragraph on the company's business.

conflicts.note: The texts are otherwise the same; the difference does not affect the event date (the 20th).
